At the very end of your answer, add one line in exactly this form, with plain numbers and no units: FINAL: finish_min=<number>; wall_risk_pct=<number>  (finish_min in minutes, wall_risk_pct in percent)

answer:
Expect to finish in about 213.5 minutes (median), with a 80% range of 207.5 to 226.8 minutes and a 95% range of 204.1 to 239.5 minutes [T1]. The model reads your pacing as a "Steady fade" [T1]. Your chance of hitting the wall, meaning a 35-40 km pace more than 25% slower than your 10-20 km pace, is about 16% (0.1645) [T1].

How far to trust this: the model was fitted on Boston splits and has no weather input. On the 2024 holdout, its 80% interval at 35 km covered only 74% of runners, so the late-race ranges are narrower than they should be [T1]. Treat the upper end (226.8 minutes and beyond) as quite possible, especially if the day is warm or windy.

What to do: (1) Hold your current effort through 30 km and don't chase time in the middle miles, since that is what drives wall risk. (2) If it is warm or windy, check the weather effect and slow your target pace to match, because this prediction ignores it.

FINAL: finish_min=213.54; wall_risk_pct=16.45
